historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (1.16%), rounded down; forward base path averages ~1.2% for FY2026-35
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-5.8% 5yr, -10.8% 3yr) diverges >30% from revenue (+1.2% 5yr) and EPS. Book value is falling because of masthead/goodwill impairments (FY2019 -$165m, FY2024 -$16m statutory loss incl. $24m impairment) and dividends above statutory earnings, not because the cash business is shrinking at that rate -- equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth anchor. EPS CAGRs are distorted by the FY2024 impairment loss and the FY2022 base (EPS in cents).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = OCF - capex - IFRS-16 lease principal - SBC (filing SBC figures). The 5-year owner-FCF CAGR is undefined because FY2020 owner FCF was negative (-$12.7m: COVID-year working-capital/tax timing, OCF only $4.2m). The +23.9% 3yr owner-FCF CAGR runs from a depressed FY2022 base ($13.2m) to the FY2025 recovery year and is NOT a growth rate to project -- it is cyclical recovery plus the $12m cost-out. Reported FCF (ex-lease) 3yr CAGR 14.0% is below owner FCF's because lease principal rose only modestly (12.0 -> 14.3) while OCF recovered; SBC is immaterial throughout.

scenario_narratives.base: Audio keeps taking share of a flat-to-slightly-growing NZ radio pool and digital subscriptions keep growing mid-single digits, but print reader and advertising revenue keep falling high-single digits, so group revenue grows ~1-2% a year -- roughly the FY2020-25 record. The FY2026 guidance ('ahead of' $62.3m Operating EBITDA) is met; the $4m+$3m AI-enabled cost-out and the new print plant lift the margin ~1.3pp by 2029, with inflation eating the rest. OneRoof stays a sub-scale #2 to Trade Me Property and contributes modest growth once the Auckland market normalises. The Google content-supply deal (expires Dec-2026) is renewed on broadly similar terms. Owner FCF dips in 2026-27 on the $15m print-plant spend, then settles around $27-30m (~7.5-8% of revenue).
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2027 cyclical recovery management is pointing to arrives: NZ ad spend and housing turnover normalise, Audio's 15-month growth streak and digital audio (+16%) compound, the new Herald app and dynamic paywall lift digital-subscription yield, and OneRoof's upgrade penetration moves toward the 60%/40% Auckland/rest-of-NZ ambition. Revenue grows 2.5-3.5% through the recovery, cost-out and print-plant savings are largely retained rather than competed away, and the Central Auckland lease resets lower -- a mature 21% EBITDA margin. Not modelled but supportive: a takeover approach from the ~20% holder or a OneRoof monetisation event.
scenario_narratives.bear: Print declines faster than digital replaces it (print subscriber volumes are already -9% YoY), the Google content-supply agreement is not renewed or renews for materially less, OneRoof's stall against Trade Me Property becomes permanent, and the mid-2026 OCR increase prolongs the NZ ad and housing downturn. Revenue shrinks ~2% a year; fixed costs (talent, print distribution, leases) do not fall as fast, so the margin slides to 15% despite the cost programmes, and the governance contest around the ~20% holder distracts management. Owner FCF falls toward ~$12-13m with no growth in perpetuity (-1% terminal).

valuation_philosophy.summary: NZME is valued as an ex-growth, cyclical cash generator, not a digital-growth story: component-built owner FCF with IFRS-16 lease payments charged in the flows (the same basis as NZME's own headline FCF), a 10.5% NZD WACC applied once, 1% base terminal growth, a 12x terminal cap and a bear-leaning 25/50/25 weighting. The recovery from the FY2024 trough and the announced cost-out programmes are credited only partially; the model does not assume the Google deal is lost in the base case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Google content-supply agreement expiry (Dec-2026) -- terms unsettled; loss is in the bear flows only
Pace of print decline versus digital subscription and audio growth
OneRoof's competitive position against Trade Me Property in a winner-take-most category
NZ advertising and housing cycle; mid-2026 OCR increase
Execution of the print-plant (up to $15m) and $7m AI cost-out programmes
Governance overhang: largest holder just under the 20% takeover threshold (upside or downside)
Recurring 'non-recurring' restructuring costs -- modelled at ~0.7pp of revenue

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 187.900m ordinary shares on issue at 31-Dec-2025 plus 1.732m dilutive performance rights (FY2025 AR note 2.3, lines 3190-3204). No shares issued in H1-2026 and no buybacks. Held FLAT because SBC (immaterial, ~0.1% of revenue) is expensed in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net BANK debt of $19.4m at 30-Jun-2026 (H1-2026 results presentation, balance-sheet slide). The interim is presentation-only and discloses the net figure, not the gross borrowings/cash split, so total_debt carries the net figure and cash is 0. FY2025 year-end split was bank loans 24.311 less cash 8.804 = 15.5. Lease liabilities ($66.6m at H1-2026) are EXCLUDED because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B); the $2.4m finance-lease (sub-lease) receivable is excluded for the same reason (sub-lease receipts are netted in the lease cost line).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report share-based payments reserve movement (line 4965: 341 thousand). NZ market: performance rights settled in shares, no net-share-settlement tax withholding disclosed. NOTE: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp for FY2021/FY2022 reads 7.1 and FY2023 1.683, which disagree with the filings (1.559, 1.683, 0.341) -- the owner-FCF history below uses the filing figures.
inputs.owner_fcf_definition: last_fcf = OCF 50.362 - capex 10.659 - IFRS-16 lease principal 14.322 - SBC 0.341 = 25.04 (FY2025). reported_fcf is CSV FreeCashFlow (OCF - capex, lease principal NOT deducted). Lease interest (4.157) is already inside OCF. NZME's own headline FCF of $25.4m is the same definition before SBC. Interest income not stripped: the company carries net debt.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T05:00:32Z regular NZX close (Yahoo Finance chart API, regularMarketTime)
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD build: NZ 10yr government ~4.5%, NZ equity risk premium ~6.0%, levered beta ~1.1 for a small-cap, advertising-cyclical media name -> cost of equity ~11.1%. Bank debt is ~9% of market cap (leases are in the flows, so not in the capital structure), after-tax cost ~4.5% -> WACC ~10.5%. One rate for all three scenarios: structural print decline, the Google-deal expiry and governance overhang are charged in the bear FLOWS and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full lease cash payment -- principal 14.322 + interest 4.157 less sub-lease principal received 0.586 ~= 17.9m in FY2025 (5.2% of operating revenue); H1-2026 7.3 + 1.9 - 0.1 = 9.1m -- is charged through lease_cost_pct_path inside EBIT. da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 30.959 - 12.240 ROU = 18.7m; H1-2026 14.5 - 5.9 = 8.6m, ~4.9% annualised) so the lease is not charged twice in the tax line. Lease liabilities excluded from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: NZME pays ~$0.4m/yr to non-controlling interests (FY2024 and FY2025 cash flow statements). No NCI share of profit is reported since FY2024; the distribution stream is capitalised at WACC and deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are not otherwise adjusted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 2: non-US operating company, cyclical, with material IFRS-16 leases). NZME is an operating media company (radio, NZ Herald, OneRoof) whose value is its free cash flow; it is not a bank/REIT/holdco and has no live takeover or scheme (Jim Grenon sits just under the 20% takeover threshold -- optionality, not a deal), so the deal-weighting row does not apply. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. CYCLICALITY: advertising and property listings are late-cycle; FY2024 (statutory EBITDA margin 14.5%) was a trough and FY2025/H1-2026 are an early recovery helped by a $12m cost-out. The base case therefore does NOT project the FY2025 recovery as the start of a re-rating; the mature statutory-equivalent EBITDA margin of 19.0% is ~1.5pp above the FY2021-25 statutory average (~17.5%), justified only by the new $4m+$3m cost-out and the ~$7m print-plant savings from 2029, with inflation absorbing part of them. EBITDA basis: Operating EBITDA (post-IFRS-16, pre-non-recurring) LESS a ~0.7pp/yr allowance for the 'non-recurring' restructuring costs NZME books almost every year (FY2024 $4.1m, FY2025 $6.0m; print-plant decommissioning in 2027 will add more). BASE REVENUE: FY2025 operating revenue incl. other income $345.1m (the denominator of the $62.3m Operating EBITDA); CSV revenue is $341.3m ex other income. CAPEX: BAU $10-12m guided for FY2026 plus the up-to-$15m print plant (~$7m 2026, ~$8m 2027). CASH TAX: 28% NZ statutory throughout -- the FY2025 $1.9m cash tax was depressed by a tax receivable carried from FY2024 overpayment, which had turned into a $2.2m payable by June 2026. WC: net working capital ex-cash is ~nil (receivables+inventory ~ payables), advertising has no deferred-revenue float of note -> wc_capture 0. SBC-ZERO market in practice (0.1% of revenue): house and street coincide, band_position is not meaningful. POST-BALANCE-DATE: the 3.0cps H1-2026 interim dividend ($5.6m) was paid 23-Sep-2026 after the 30-June net-debt date and the shares already trade ex; it is deducted in the equity bridge. DIVIDEND CONTEXT: 9.0cps FY2025 = 8.5% cash yield at the current price, paid within a 50-80%-of-FCF policy -- the market is pricing NZME as an ex-growth yield stock.
inputs.cyclicality_note: Mid-cycle anchoring rather than a normalised historical FCF: owner FCF over FY2021-25 averaged ~$19.8m (33.0, 13.2, 17.0, 11.0, 25.0), so FY2025's $25.0m is at the upper end of the 5-year range. The base case's first explicit years are BELOW FY2025 owner FCF because of the print-plant capex and a full cash-tax year, recovering to ~$27-30m only once the cost programmes land.

base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: FY2026: Operating EBITDA guided 'ahead of' $62.3m; H1 +11% to $26.5m -> ~$64m on ~$348.6m revenue = 18.4%, less ~0.7pp recurring 'non-recurring' costs = 17.7%. FY2027: $4m cost-out at full run-rate + half of the $3m second tranche, offset by print-plant transition/redundancy costs. FY2028-29: print-plant savings $3-5m then ~$7m and the full $3m tranche, with wage/newsprint inflation absorbing roughly half. Mature 19.0% statutory-equivalent (~19.7% Operating).
base.lease_cost_pct_path_rationale: FY2025 lease cash ~$17.9m net of sub-lease receipts (5.2%). Central Auckland lease renegotiated on 'materially improved terms' (Heads of Terms backdated to Nov-2025, pending approval) and lease liabilities running down (79.8 -> 71.7 -> 66.6) -> ~flat nominal lease cash on growing revenue, 4.8% from FY2029.
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: FY2026 BAU $11m + print plant $7m = $18m; FY2027 BAU ~$11.5m + $8m; thereafter BAU ~3.4% of revenue (FY2025 3.1%, FY2024 3.7%). D&A ex-ROU glides from 4.9% down to capex parity (3.5%) as acquired-intangible/software amortisation rolls off.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: print is in structural decline, the Google deal expires in December 2026 with terms unsettled, OneRoof has stalled against an entrenched #1, and management itself calls H2-2026 'volatile'. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs a macro recovery, OneRoof share gains and retained cost savings all at once, though the cyclical-trough setting and the ~20% holder's takeover optionality keep it from going lower. Base 50%: guidance for FY2026 is credible given H1's +11% EBITDA.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: Band collapsed: SBC is ~0.1% of revenue ($0.34m), so house and street values differ by ~NZ$0.02/share and the band-position ratio is numerically meaningless (the price sits well outside a two-cent band). Reported as null per the SBC-zero rule.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
